balances.name: Energy pays for the exhaust
balances.near_c: gamma - 1 <= fuel_j_per_kg / c^2 for the exhaust's speed (the relativistic form)
balances.catches: a chemical fuel with a torch's exhaust speed
balances.says: the exhaust is {times} times as fast as its fuel's energy can make it

check.name: Fastest exhaust the fuel's energy can pay for
check.formula:
g = 1 + fuel_j_per_kg / c^2
supply = c * sqrt(1 - 1 / g^2)
demand = exhaust_km_s

source.text: Einstein 1905, kinetic energy (gamma - 1) m c^2 of a moving mass; below a few per cent of c it is the familiar half m v^2

explain.curious: Throwing exhaust takes energy. If every joule in the fuel went into the jet, this is the fastest it could leave.
explain.science: (gamma - 1) c^2 <= E per kg thrown, so v <= c sqrt(1 - 1/(1 + E/c^2)^2); for E much less than c^2, v <= sqrt(2E).

balances.name: Jet power
balances.catches: thrust and exhaust speed set apart that need more power than the ship makes
balances.says: the jet needs {times} times the power the plant gives

plant_w.name: power the plant gives the drive

explain.curious: A jet carries energy away as fast as it leaves. Something on board has to make that much power.
explain.science: Jet power is half the thrust times the exhaust speed (thrust = mass flow x speed, power = half mass flow x speed squared).

balances.name: Energy in, energy out
balances.catches: waste heat set to nothing while the plant's efficiency says otherwise
balances.says: {times} times as much power goes out as comes in

check.name: Power out against power in
check.formula:
demand = jet_w + waste_w + stored_w + loads_w
supply = plant_w

explain.curious: Every watt the plant makes goes somewhere: the jet, waste heat, a store or the ship's other loads.
explain.science: Plant output = jet power + waste heat + power stored + other loads, within 2 per cent.

balances.name: Momentum
balances.relation: thrust_n = mdot_kg_s * exhaust_km_s * 1000, or thrust_n <= plant_w * unthrown_n_per_w for light alone
balances.catches: thrust with nothing thrown and no stated partner
balances.says: the thrust is {times} times what is thrown can give

check.name: Thrust what is thrown can give
check.formula:
demand = thrust_n
supply = mdot_kg_s * exhaust_km_s + plant_w / c

plant_w.name: power thrown as light, if any

supply.name: thrust the mass and light thrown give

explain.curious: To push forward, a ship has to throw something back. With nothing thrown and no partner named, there is no thrust.
explain.science: Thrust is at most mass flow x exhaust speed, plus P/c for power thrown as light.

balances.name: Heat flows downhill
balances.relation: radiator_k <= waste_heat_k, unless a heat pump is paid for: pump_w >= q_w * (t_hot_k - t_cold_k) / t_cold_k, and pump_w is shed too
balances.catches: a hot radiator cooling a cool room for free
balances.says: heat is pushed uphill with {times} times the pump work paid for

check.name: Work to pump heat uphill to the radiators
check.formula:
demand = if radiator_k > waste_heat_k then q_w * (radiator_k - waste_heat_k) / waste_heat_k else 0
supply = pump_w

source.text: Clausius 1854: heat passes of itself only from hotter to colder; the least work to lift heat Q from T_cold to T_hot is Q (T_hot - T_cold) / T_cold

explain.curious: Heat runs downhill. A radiator hotter than what it cools needs a heat pump, and the pump's work is more heat to shed.
explain.science: W >= Q (T_r - T_s) / T_s when T_r > T_s, else nothing (Carnot coefficient of performance).
